answer: The protocol requires each new agent to solve a verifiable delay function (VDF) seeded with a unique hash of a walnut‑derived salt and a cedar‑derived nonce, producing an ember‑colored proof that can only be verified after a wall‑clock delay of T minutes. Because VDF evaluation is inherently sequential, an attacker must allocate a dedicated CPU core for the full delay per identity, cannot parallelise, and must also lock up a stake of 5 ETH that is forfeited if the proof is later invalidated.
